bands.label: Renewed strikes after Eid pause
bands.summary: An Eid-ul-Fitr pause collapses as Pakistani airstrikes hit eastern Afghanistan, the Taliban claims 13 civilians killed including children, and Afghan forces stage retaliatory attacks along the Durand Line.

bands.label: Post-Taliban return tensions
bands.summary: After the Taliban retake Kabul, TTP attacks inside Pakistan rise sharply, Islamabad conducts repeated cross-border strikes, and Afghan-Pakistani relations cycle through clashes, fence disputes, and short ceasefires.

frames.label: June 2026 strikes
frames.note: Story begins when Pakistani airstrikes hit Kunar and other eastern districts after a month of relative calm following the Eid pause, killing civilians the Taliban administration counts as 13 including 11 children. Under this frame the situation reads as a sudden rupture of a fragile ceasefire and a new round of cross-border fire. This is the frame most wire reports and Indian outlets like DD News and News On AIR open with.

frames.label: Aug 2021 Taliban return
frames.note: Story begins when the Taliban retook Kabul and TTP attacks on Pakistani soil escalated, with Islamabad arguing militants now operate freely from Afghan territory. Under this frame the strikes read as counterterrorism against a neighbor harboring armed groups, and Afghan retaliation reads as state sponsorship surfacing. This is the frame Pakistani security commentary in Daily Times and Press TV opens with.
